question: Do candidate-specific support breadth, concentration and timing from recent and pending-cart items improve ranking beyond the frozen 134-feature representation?
candidate_generation: reuse exact saved candidate IDs; no retrieval changes
folds: Reuse exact saved two forward query-time folds; six-hour query embargo; censor training labels at validation start before negatives are sampled
model: LightGBM LambdaRank; unchanged prior pilot parameters; 150 rounds
control: 134-feature shared model's saved per-session hits, verified by S3 object versions and input/fold provenance; zero control refits
metric: 0.1 clicks + 0.3 carts + 0.6 orders; sum hits at 20 / sum min(20, full distinct truth count) per objective
bootstrap: 1000 paired session replicates stratified by forward fold; exploratory unadjusted 95% intervals
replication_gate: Pooled gain >= 0.003, nonnegative gain on both folds, and no pooled order-recall loss. If interval includes zero, classify as promising point estimate only. Never auto-promote.
preflight: Existing .venv, exact Git source and saved artifacts; 16-session feature replay before further materialization; each completed chunk/model checkpoint reused
interpretation: Previously used fitting data. Not a leaderboard score, untouched holdout, proof of deployment readiness or evidence that 0.60503 has been beaten.
